description: Read one Ptitchef recipe: its ingredients, method, times, rating, nutrition and the cost the site estimates for it. Pass the 'id' of a row from search_recipes, browse_recipes or search_by_ingredients. Give 'servings' to rescale the ingredients, and read each line's 'scaling' before quoting a quantity: 'scaled' is exact arithmetic, 'rounded' was moved to stay usable, and 'unscaled' carries nothing that could be multiplied. A time or a figure the site publishes none of comes back null, never zero.

id.description: The 'id' of a row from a search or a listing, which is the recipe's own page path.

servings.description: Rescale the ingredients to this many servings. Left out, the ingredients come back as published.

name: get_recipe

difficulty.description: The site's own wording, such as 'facile'.

estimated_cost.description: What the site estimates the ingredients cost, with the currency it names. Repeated as published: it is the site's figure and readers of the site dispute it.

image_url.description: The photograph the site took of this step.

ingredients.description: The lines as published where no servings were asked for, in which case 'yield.factor' is null and each line's 'scaling' describes no arithmetic. Pass 'servings' to rescale them.

adjusted.description: True when rounding moved the value away from the exact product, which is what makes a line 'rounded' rather than 'scaled'.

amount.description: The scaled quantity, expressed in 'unit'. Read the two together: a large result is moved to a bigger unit, so 200 g scaled tenfold reads as 2 kg, and the bare number shrinks while the quantity grows.

amount_max.description: Upper bound when the line gives a range, as in '200 à 300 g', with 'amount' holding the lower one. Null when the line states a single amount.

note.description: Why the line was rounded, clamped or left alone, including when the measure is approximate and only its count was multiplied.

original.description: The ingredient line exactly as Ptitchef publishes it.

scaling.description: 'scaled' means the arithmetic came out exact, which a count reaches as readily as a mass: one pincée multiplied by six is six pincées. 'rounded' means the value had to be moved to stay usable, to a whole or half unit or to a step a scale can show. 'unscaled' was left as published, because nothing on the line is the factor's to multiply: the note says which of the two it is.

text.description: The line after scaling, identical to 'original' when unscaled.

unit.description: The unit 'amount' is in, which may differ from the one the recipe used.

notes.description: What qualifies this answer: what the arithmetic did, what it could not do, and what the site states rather than this server. Read these before quoting a quantity or a cost.

serving_size.description: The serving the figures below describe.

nutrition.description: As published, per the serving size it names.

rating.description: 1 to 5, as the site states it.

source.description: The site this recipe was read from. Credit it when showing it.

steps.description: The method, one line per step, in the shape every source of recipes publishes it in. 'illustrated_steps' carries the same lines beside the photograph the site took of each.

steps_are_one_block.description: True when the site published its method as one block of prose, so the single step above is that block rather than the first of several.

translations.description: The other languages this recipe was published in, which get_recipe_translations answers on its own for a caller who wants nothing else.

url.description: The public page. Show this when citing the recipe.

factor.description: What the ingredients were multiplied by. Null where none was applied: no servings were asked for, or the page states none to divide by.

original_text.description: The page's own wording for them.

unit.description: What the page counts its servings in, in its own wording: 'personnes' on one recipe and 'pièces' on another. Null where it states a bare number, and 'servings' then means whatever that number counts.

title: Read one recipe
